source.text: בֶּן־שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים יְהוֹאָ֥שׁ בְּמָלְכֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [A] son of seven years [was] Jehoash when he became king.

en.L: A son of seven years [was] Jehoash when he became king.
en.B: Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.
en.R: Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: in the Hebrew text this verse begins chapter 12
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 11 ends with the crowning of Jehoash and the death of Athaliah (11:20), and this verse, giving the young king's age, begins chapter 12. Many Bibles number it 11:21 and so number the rest of this chapter (12:2-22 here) 12:1-21. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: a son of seven years: seven years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being the son of so many years. Jehoash had been hidden in the temple for six years while Athaliah ruled (11:3), and Jehoiada made him king in the seventh (11:4, 12).

decisions.choice: Jehoash: the same king called Joash
decisions.reason: The name means "Yahweh has given". Kings uses the longer form Jehoash for him in this chapter until verse 20, and the shorter form Joash in 11:2 and in verses 20-21; both name the one king of Judah, son of Ahaziah (11:2).

decisions.choice: Jehoash was seven years old
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the age as English does and put the name first; Literal keeps the Hebrew order and idiom.

source.text: בִּשְׁנַת־שֶׁ֤בַע לְיֵהוּא֙ מָלַ֣ךְ יְהוֹאָ֔שׁ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ צִבְיָ֖ה מִבְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

records.literal_gloss: In year seven of Jehu became king Jehoash, and forty year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem, and [the] name of his mother [was] Zibiah from Beersheba.

en.L: In [the] seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king, and forty years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Zibiah from Beersheba.
en.B: In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah from Beersheba.
en.R: Jehoash became king in the seventh year that Jehu was king of Israel. He ruled in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother was Zibiah from Beersheba.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: this is verse 1 of chapter 12 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text this is verse 2, because the Hebrew chapter begins one verse earlier (see verse 1). Many Bibles number this verse 12:1 and the following verses one lower than here, through 12:21 for verse 22.

decisions.choice: the seventh year of Jehu: dated by the reign of the king of Israel
decisions.reason: As Kings does for each reign, the start of Jehoash's reign in Judah is dated by the year of the king ruling in Israel. Jehu had come to power when he killed Joram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah on the same day (9:24, 27), and Athaliah then ruled Judah for six years (11:3).

decisions.choice: his mother's name: the queen mother named in the formula
decisions.reason: For the kings of Judah the formula names the king's mother (1 Kings 15:2), who held a place of her own at court. Beersheba lay in the far south of Judah (1 Kings 5:5).

decisions.choice: two sentences, the date first named as Jehu's reign over Israel
decisions.reason: Readable splits the formula into short sentences, as these books allow, and names Israel so the reader knows which kingdom Jehu ruled.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יְהוֹאָ֧שׁ הַיָּשָׁ֛ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כָּל־יָמָ֑יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹרָ֔הוּ יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And did Jehoash the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh all his days which instructed him Jehoiada the priest.

en.L: And Jehoash did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
en.B: Jehoash did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
en.R: Jehoash did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right all his days, because Jehoiada the priest taught him.

decisions.choice: did what was right in Yahweh's eyes: the good verdict
decisions.reason: This is the good verdict of the regnal formula, given to the kings of Judah who were faithful to Yahweh (1 Kings 15:11). Verse 4 adds the one thing that held it back.

decisions.choice: all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him
alternatives: all his days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him
as long as Jehoiada the priest instructed him
decisions.reason: The linking word can give the reason ("because") or limit the time ("all his days in which"). Read the first way, the verdict covers Jehoash's whole reign and names Jehoiada's teaching as what made it so. Read the second way, the verdict holds only for the years while Jehoiada taught him. 2 Chronicles 24:2 says he did right "all the days of Jehoiada the priest", and 2 Chronicles 24:17-22 tells how he turned away after Jehoiada died, which fits the second reading. Kings itself tells of no such turning.

decisions.choice: instructed: taught him the right way
decisions.reason: The verb means to teach or direct, the word from which torah, "instruction", comes. Jehoiada the priest had saved the boy, made him king and made the covenant between Yahweh, the king and the people (11:4-17).

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The good verdict is worded the same way at each level throughout these books. "All his days" is kept at every level so that the question in m2 stays open; "taught" at Readable is the common word for "instructed".

source.text: רַ֥ק הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא־סָ֑רוּ ע֥וֹד הָעָ֛ם מְזַבְּחִ֥ים וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים בַּבָּמֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Only the high places not were removed; still the people [were] sacrificing and burning incense at the high places.

en.L: Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense at the high places.
en.B: The high places, however, were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.
en.R: But the hilltop shrines were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the hilltop shrines.

decisions.choice: the high places were not removed: the reservation in the good verdict
decisions.reason: The high places were local places of worship. Kings counts it against even the good kings of Judah that they left them standing (1 Kings 15:14; 22:44), until Hezekiah and Josiah removed them (18:4; 23:8). The verb does not say who should have removed them.

decisions.choice: burning incense: or burning offerings so that their smoke rose
alternatives: making offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke. It is used both of burning incense and of burning offerings on an altar; here, beside "sacrificing", it may mean either.

decisions.choice: high places (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹאָ֜שׁ אֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים כֹּל֩ כֶּ֨סֶף הַקֳּדָשִׁ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־יוּבָ֤א בֵית־יְהוָה֙ כֶּ֣סֶף עוֹבֵ֔ר אִ֕ישׁ כֶּ֥סֶף נַפְשׁ֖וֹת עֶרְכּ֑וֹ כָּל־כֶּ֗סֶף אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַֽעֲלֶה֙ עַ֣ל לֶב־אִ֔ישׁ לְהָבִ֖יא בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jehoash to the priests, all [the] money of the holy things which is brought [into the] house of Yahweh, money passing, [each] man money of persons his valuation, all money which comes up on [the] heart of [a] man to bring [into the] house of Yahweh,

en.L: And Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money of the holy things that is brought [into the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, money of [one] passing [over], the money of persons, each [at] his valuation, all the money that comes up on [the] heart of a man to bring [into the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money from the holy gifts that is brought into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the money of those who are counted, the money for persons at the value set for each, and all the money anyone is moved to bring into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.R: Jehoash said to the priests, "People bring money to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as holy gifts. Some is the tax paid by each one who is counted. Some is paid when people make vows, at the price set for each person. And some is money people freely choose to bring to the temple.

decisions.choice: the money of the holy things: money given to the temple as holy
decisions.reason: Holy things are gifts set apart for Yahweh and so belonging to the temple (1 Kings 15:15). The king names three kinds of such money in the rest of the verse.

decisions.choice: money of one passing over: the half-shekel paid by each one counted in a census
decisions.reason: The phrase is "money passing". The law says that everyone who "passes over" to those being counted is to give a half-shekel to Yahweh for the work of the tent of meeting (Exodus 30:12-16), and 2 Chronicles 24:6, 9 speaks of the tax Moses laid on Israel. The same words in Genesis 23:16 mean silver that passes in trade, that is, current money, and some read them that way here, as a heading for the money that follows.

decisions.choice: money of persons at his valuation: the price set for a person vowed to Yahweh
decisions.reason: Leviticus 27:2-8 lets someone who has vowed a person to Yahweh pay a set value instead, fixed by age and sex. This money came to the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: comes up on the heart of a man: what anyone freely decides to give
decisions.reason: Something "comes up on the heart" when a person thinks of it or chooses it. These are freewill gifts, given without any law requiring them (Exodus 35:21).

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 6
decisions.reason: The verse lists the money; verse 6 says what the priests are to do with it. The king's words run from here to the end of verse 6.

decisions.choice: the tax paid by each one who is counted; paid when people make vows
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two kinds of money (m2, m3) and turns the list into short sentences.

source.text: יִקְח֤וּ לָהֶם֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֵ֣ת מַכָּר֑וֹ וְהֵ֗ם יְחַזְּקוּ֙ אֶת־בֶּ֣דֶק הַבַּ֔יִת לְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יִמָּצֵ֥א שָׁ֖ם בָּֽדֶק׃פ

records.literal_gloss: let take for themselves the priests, each from with his acquaintance, and they shall repair the breach of the house for all which is found there breach.

en.L: let the priests take [it] for themselves, each from his acquaintance, and they shall repair the breach of the house, wherever any breach is found."
en.B: let the priests take it, each from the people he knows, and let them repair the damage to the house wherever any damage is found."
en.R: The priests are to receive it, each one from the people he knows, and they must repair the temple wherever they find damage."

decisions.choice: his acquaintance: a person the priest knew; perhaps a donor or a temple assessor
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and in verse 8. It comes from the verb "to know" or "to recognize", so it most likely means someone the priest knew: the worshipers each priest dealt with brought their money to him. Others take it to name a temple official who valued the gifts, or the donor himself. What the word means for the story is clear in any case: the money passed through the priests' own hands.

decisions.choice: breach: damage to the building needing repair
decisions.reason: The word means a breach or crack, and so any part of the building that had broken down. Athaliah's sons had broken into the house of God and used its holy things for the Baals (2 Chronicles 24:7).

decisions.choice: let the priests take: the king's command
decisions.reason: The verb is a command in the third person. The priests were to receive the money and themselves see to the repairs.

decisions.choice: the people he knows
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the people he knows" for the uncertain word (m1); Literal keeps "acquaintance".

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְשָׁלֹ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יְהוֹאָ֑שׁ לֹֽא־חִזְּק֥וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֶת־בֶּ֥דֶק הַבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in year twenty and three year of the king Jehoash, not had repaired the priests the breach of the house.

en.L: And it was in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests had not repaired the breach of the house.
en.B: But by the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests still had not repaired the damage to the house.
en.R: But by the time King Jehoash had been ruling for twenty-three years, the priests had still not repaired the temple.

decisions.choice: the twenty-third year: Jehoash was about thirty
decisions.reason: Jehoash became king at seven (verse 1), so in his twenty-third year he was about thirty. The verse does not say when he gave his order (verses 5-6), but by now the priests had had years to do the work.

decisions.choice: But ... still
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "but" and "still" to show what the Hebrew order implies: the work ordered in verse 6 had not been done.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָא֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ יְהוֹאָ֜שׁ לִיהוֹיָדָ֤ע הַכֹּהֵן֙ וְלַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם מַדּ֛וּעַ אֵינְכֶ֥ם מְחַזְּקִ֖ים אֶת־בֶּ֣דֶק הַבָּ֑יִת וְעַתָּ֗ה אַל־תִּקְחוּ־כֶ֨סֶף֙ מֵאֵ֣ת מַכָּֽרֵיכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־לְבֶ֥דֶק הַבַּ֖יִת תִּתְּנֻֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And summoned the king Jehoash Jehoiada the priest and the priests, and he said to them, why? not you repairing the breach of the house; and now not take money from with your acquaintances, for for [the] breach of the house you shall give it.

en.L: And King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the priests, and he said to them, "Why are you not repairing the breach of the house? And now, do not take money from your acquaintances, but for the breach of the house you shall give it."
en.B: So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the house? From now on take no more money from the people you know. Hand it over for the damage to the house."
en.R: So King Jehoash called for Jehoiada the priest and the other priests. He asked them, "Why are you not repairing the temple? From now on, do not take any more money from the people you know. Hand it over to pay for the repairs."

decisions.choice: your acquaintances: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The same uncertain word as in verse 6, now in the plural.

decisions.choice: but you shall give it for the breach: the priests are to pass the money on
decisions.reason: "It" is the money. The king does not take the money away from the temple; he takes it out of the priests' hands, so that it goes straight to the repairs (verses 9-16). It may include what the priests already held.

decisions.choice: Jehoiada the priest: the chief priest
decisions.reason: Jehoiada had led the overthrow of Athaliah (chapter 11). He is the chief of the priests, so the king speaks to him and to the priests under him.

decisions.choice: the other priests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the other priests" because Jehoiada is one of them.

source.text: וַיֵּאֹ֖תוּ הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֑ים לְבִלְתִּ֤י קְחַת־כֶּ֨סֶף֙ מֵאֵ֣ת הָעָ֔ם וּלְבִלְתִּ֥י חַזֵּ֖ק אֶת־בֶּ֥דֶק הַבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: And agreed the priests to not take money from with the people and to not repair the breach of the house.

en.L: And the priests agreed not to take money from the people and not to repair the breach of the house.
en.B: The priests agreed that they would take no more money from the people and would not be the ones to repair the damage to the house.
en.R: The priests agreed not to take any more money from the people. They also agreed that they would no longer be in charge of repairing the temple.

decisions.choice: not to repair: they gave up the task of repairing
decisions.reason: The priests did not refuse to have the temple repaired. They gave up both the money and the duty of doing the repairs, which now passed to others (verses 10-12).

decisions.choice: would not be the ones to repair; would no longer be in charge of repairing
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the agreement meant (m1), so the reader does not take it that the priests refused to let the work be done.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֞ח יְהוֹיָדָ֤ע הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֲר֣וֹן אֶחָ֔ד וַיִּקֹּ֥ב חֹ֖ר בְּדַלְתּ֑וֹ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֹתוֹ֩ אֵ֨צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ מִיָּמִ֗ין בְּבֽוֹא־אִישׁ֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְנָֽתְנוּ־שָׁ֤מָּה הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ שֹׁמְרֵ֣י הַסַּ֔ף אֶת־כָּל־הַכֶּ֖סֶף הַמּוּבָ֥א בֵית־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Jehoiada the priest a chest one, and he bored a hole in its lid, and he put it beside the altar on [the] right as comes [one] [into the] house of Yahweh; and put there the priests keeping the threshold all the money brought [into the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Jehoiada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in its lid, and he put it beside the altar, on the right as one comes into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and the priests who kept the threshold put there all the money that was brought [into the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest and drilled a hole in its lid. He placed it next to the altar, on the right side as people enter the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The priests who guarded the doorway put into it all the money brought into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then Jehoiada the priest took a wooden chest and made a hole in its lid. He placed it beside the altar, on the right side as people come into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The priests who guarded the entrance put into the chest all the money that people brought to the temple.

decisions.choice: a chest: a box for the money, with a hole in its lid
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the ark of the covenant and for a coffin (Genesis 50:26); here it is a plain box. With a hole bored in the lid, money could be put in but not taken out, so it was kept safe until it was counted (verse 11).

decisions.choice: on the right: the reading in the margin
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text read "on the right", and the reading in the margin "from the right", that is, on the right side. Both mean the same place.

decisions.choice: the priests who kept the threshold: the doorkeepers of the temple
decisions.reason: These priests guarded the entrance to the temple (22:4; 25:18). People handed their money to them at the door, and the priests put it into the chest. The altar here is most likely the bronze altar in the courtyard before the temple.

decisions.choice: doorway (Balanced); entrance (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the place the threshold stands for; Literal keeps "threshold".

decisions.choice: a wooden chest
decisions.reason: Readable adds "wooden" because a lid and a bored hole imply a box of wood, and a modern reader may not picture what kind of chest is meant.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּרְאוֹתָ֔ם כִּֽי־רַ֥ב הַכֶּ֖סֶף בָּֽאָר֑וֹן וַיַּ֨עַל סֹפֵ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְהַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל וַיָּצֻ֨רוּ֙ וַיִּמְנ֔וּ אֶת־הַכֶּ֖סֶף הַנִּמְצָ֥א בֵית־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when they saw that much [was] the money in the chest, and came up [the] scribe of the king and the priest the great, and they tied up and counted the money found [in the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And it was, when they saw that the money in the chest [was] much, the scribe of the king and the high priest came up, and they tied [it] up and counted the money that was found [in the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Each time they saw that the chest held a large sum, the king's secretary and the high priest came up. They tied up in bags the money found in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and counted it.
en.R: Whenever they saw that the chest held a lot of money, the king's secretary and the high priest came to the temple. They counted the money that was found in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and tied it up in bags.

decisions.choice: the king's scribe: the royal secretary
decisions.reason: The scribe was one of the king's chief officials, who kept records and handled royal business (2 Samuel 8:17; 1 Kings 4:3). His presence beside the high priest made sure the money was counted openly, by the palace and the temple together.

decisions.choice: the high priest: literally "the great priest"
decisions.reason: This is the title of the chief priest (Leviticus 21:10), at this time Jehoiada (verse 10).

decisions.choice: they tied it up: bound the silver in bags
decisions.reason: The verb means to tie up or bind, and is used of silver tied in bags (5:23). The parallel in 22:9 uses a verb meaning to pour out. Some take the word here from a root meaning to cast metal, so that the silver was melted into bars, but nothing else in the story suggests this.

decisions.choice: counted ... and tied it up in bags
decisions.reason: Readable puts the counting first, as English expects; the Hebrew joins the two actions with "and" without saying which came first.

source.text: וְנָתְנוּ֙ אֶת־הַכֶּ֣סֶף הַֽמְתֻכָּ֔ן עַל־יְדֵי֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה הַמֻּפְקָדִ֖ים בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיּוֹצִיאֻ֜הוּ לְחָרָשֵׁ֤י הָעֵץ֙ וְלַבֹּנִ֔ים הָעֹשִׂ֖ים בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they put the money weighed out on [the] hands of [the] doers of the work, those appointed [over the] house of Yahweh, and they paid it out to [the] craftsmen of the wood and to the builders, those working [on the] house of Yahweh,

en.L: And they gave the money that was weighed out into the hands of the doers of the work, who were appointed over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they paid it out to the craftsmen in wood and to the builders who were working on the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: Then they gave the weighed money to the men doing the work, who had been put in charge of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. These paid it out to the carpenters and the builders who were working on the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.R: Then they weighed the money and gave it to the men who had been put in charge of the work on the temple. These men used it to pay the carpenters and builders who were working on the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: weighed out: silver measured by weight
decisions.reason: There were no coins yet in Judah. Silver was weighed out for each payment, so counting the money meant weighing it.

decisions.choice: the hands of ... those appointed: the reading in the margin
decisions.reason: In two places the letters written in the Hebrew text differ slightly from the reading given in the margin: "his hand" for "the hands", and another form of the word for those appointed. The record follows the margin; the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the doers of the work: the overseers, who paid the workmen
decisions.reason: The men who received the money are described as "those appointed over the house". They were in charge of the work and paid the craftsmen who did it (verse 16).

decisions.choice: the list goes on into verse 13
decisions.reason: Verse 13 goes on with the rest of the workmen and the materials paid for.

decisions.choice: carpenters
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "carpenters" for "craftsmen of the wood".

source.text: וְלַגֹּֽדְרִים֙ וּלְחֹצְבֵ֣י הָאֶ֔בֶן וְלִקְנ֤וֹת עֵצִים֙ וְאַבְנֵ֣י מַחְצֵ֔ב לְחַזֵּ֖ק אֶת־בֶּ֣דֶק בֵּית־יְהוָ֑ה וּלְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵ֥א עַל־הַבַּ֖יִת לְחָזְקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and to the masons and to [the] hewers of the stone, and to buy timber and stones of hewing to repair the breach of [the] house of Yahweh, and for all which went out on the house to repair [it].

en.L: and to the masons and to the hewers of stone, and to buy timber and hewn stones to repair the breach of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and for all that went out on the house for repairing [it].
en.B: and to the masons and the stonecutters. With it they also bought timber and dressed stone for mending the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and paid every other cost of the repairs.
en.R: They also paid the masons and the stonecutters. They bought wood and cut stone to repair the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they paid for everything else the repairs cost.

decisions.choice: masons: builders of walls
decisions.reason: The word is from a verb meaning to build a wall. These are the men who laid stone, set beside those who cut it.

decisions.choice: stones of hewing: stone cut and shaped in the quarry
decisions.reason: The temple was built of stone dressed at the quarry (1 Kings 5:31; 6:7).

decisions.choice: all that went out on the house: every expense of the repairs
decisions.reason: Money "goes out" when it is spent. The phrase takes in whatever else the work cost.

decisions.choice: With it they also bought
decisions.reason: Balanced starts a new sentence with "with it they also bought" so the list of payments reads clearly.

source.text: אַךְ֩ לֹ֨א יֵעָשֶׂ֜ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֗ה סִפּ֥וֹת כֶּ֨סֶף֙ מְזַמְּר֤וֹת מִזְרָקוֹת֙ חֲצֹ֣צְר֔וֹת כָּל־כְּלִ֥י זָהָ֖ב וּכְלִי־כָ֑סֶף מִן־הַכֶּ֖סֶף הַמּוּבָ֥א בֵית־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Only not were made [for the] house of Yahweh basins of silver, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, any vessel of gold and vessel of silver, from the money brought [into the] house of Yahweh,

en.L: But there were not made [for the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} basins of silver, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, any vessel of gold or vessel of silver, from the money that was brought [into the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: But none of the money brought into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was used to make silver basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any other articles of gold or silver for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.R: But the money brought to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not used to make gold or silver objects for the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. No silver bowls, tools for trimming lamps, bowls for sprinkling, or trumpets were made from it.

decisions.choice: basins, snuffers, bowls, trumpets: the metal articles used in temple worship
decisions.reason: These are the vessels and tools of the temple service: basins, trimmers for the lamp wicks, bowls for sprinkling blood, and silver trumpets for the priests (1 Kings 7:50; Numbers 10:2, 8).

decisions.choice: not made from the money: all of it went to the repairs
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 24:14 adds that when the repairs were finished, the money left over was used to make articles for the temple. Kings speaks only of the time the work was going on.

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 15
decisions.reason: Verse 15 gives the reason: the money was given to the workmen.

decisions.choice: wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the snuffers and bowls were for; Literal keeps the shorter names.

source.text: כִּֽי־לְעֹשֵׂ֥י הַמְּלָאכָ֖ה יִתְּנֻ֑הוּ וְחִזְּקוּ־ב֖וֹ אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: for to [the] doers of the work they gave it, and they repaired with it [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: for they gave it to the doers of the work, and with it they repaired the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: for it was given to the men doing the work, who used it to repair the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Instead, it was given to the men doing the work, and they used it to repair the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: they gave it: the money was given; no one is named
decisions.reason: "They" is general, the people handling the money (verses 11-12); the point is where the money went.

decisions.choice: Instead
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence and says "instead" for the linking word, showing that this verse answers verse 14.

source.text: וְלֹ֧א יְחַשְּׁב֣וּ אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתְּנ֤וּ אֶת־הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ עַל־יָדָ֔ם לָתֵ֖ת לְעֹשֵׂ֣י הַמְּלָאכָ֑ה כִּ֥י בֶאֱמֻנָ֖ה הֵ֥ם עֹשִֽׂים׃

records.literal_gloss: And not they settled accounts with the men whom they gave the money on their hand to give to [the] doers of the work, for in faithfulness they [were] acting.

en.L: And they did not settle accounts with the men into whose hand they gave the money to give to the doers of the work, for they acted in faithfulness.
en.B: No accounting was asked of the men who were handed the money to pay the workmen, because those men dealt honestly.
en.R: No one asked the men who paid the workers to give an account of the money, because they were honest.

decisions.choice: settle accounts: ask for a reckoning of how the money was spent
decisions.reason: The verb means to count or reckon. No one checked the overseers' accounts, because they could be trusted.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness: honestly, trustworthily
decisions.reason: The word means steadiness and reliability, someone who can be trusted. Here it is honesty with money. 22:7 says the same of the workmen under Josiah.

decisions.choice: they acted: the men who received the money
decisions.reason: "They" are the men who were handed the money, the overseers of verse 12.

decisions.choice: those men
decisions.reason: Balanced says "those men" for "they" (m3), so the honesty is not taken as the workmen's.

source.text: כֶּ֤סֶף אָשָׁם֙ וְכֶ֣סֶף חַטָּא֔וֹת לֹ֥א יוּבָ֖א בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יִהְיֽוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Money of guilt offering and money of sin offerings not was brought [into the] house of Yahweh; to the priests they belonged.

en.L: Money of guilt offering and money of sin offerings was not brought [into the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; to the priests it belonged.
en.B: The money from guilt offerings and from sin offerings did not go into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It was for the priests.
en.R: But the money from guilt offerings and sin offerings was not brought into the temple for the repairs. It belonged to the priests.

decisions.choice: money of guilt offering and of sin offerings: payments made with these offerings
decisions.reason: When someone wronged Yahweh or another person, the law required repayment with a fifth added, which went to the priest along with the guilt offering (Leviticus 5:16; Numbers 5:8). Money linked with the sin offerings may have been paid in the same way. The priests lived from such shares (Leviticus 7:7).

decisions.choice: not brought into the house: not put into the chest
decisions.reason: In this story money "brought into the house" is money put in the chest for the repairs (verses 10, 14). This money stayed with the priests, as the law gave it to them.

decisions.choice: for the repairs
decisions.reason: Readable says what "brought into the temple" means in this story (m2).

source.text: אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֗ה חֲזָאֵל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם וַיִּלָּ֥חֶם עַל־גַּ֖ת וַֽיִּלְכְּדָ֑הּ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם חֲזָאֵל֙ פָּנָ֔יו לַעֲל֖וֹת עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Then went up Hazael king of Aram and fought against Gath and captured it; and set Hazael his face to go up against Jerusalem.

en.L: Then Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it; and Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
en.B: At that time Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it. Then Hazael turned to go up against Jerusalem.
en.R: About that time Hazael king of Aram attacked the city of Gath and captured it. Then he decided to attack Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: then: at about that time
decisions.reason: The word ties the story loosely to Jehoash's reign; it does not say how long after the repairs it happened.

decisions.choice: Hazael king of Aram; Gath
decisions.reason: Hazael had seized the throne of Aram in Damascus (8:7-15) and pressed hard on Israel (10:32-33). Gath was one of the Philistine cities, west of Judah near its border. Taking it opened the way to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: set his face: turned with the firm purpose to go
decisions.reason: To set one's face toward a place is to resolve to go there (Jeremiah 42:15).

decisions.choice: turned to go up (Balanced); decided to attack (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m3); Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֞ח יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֗ה אֵ֣ת כָּל־הַקֳּדָשִׁ֡ים אֲשֶׁר־הִקְדִּ֣ישׁוּ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט וִיהוֹרָם֩ וַאֲחַזְיָ֨הוּ אֲבֹתָ֜יו מַלְכֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ וְאֶת־קֳדָשָׁ֔יו וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־הַזָּהָ֗ב הַנִּמְצָ֛א בְּאֹצְר֥וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח לַֽחֲזָאֵל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם וַיַּ֖עַל מֵעַ֥ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Jehoash king of Judah all the holy things which had consecrated Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah his fathers, kings of Judah, and his holy things, and all the gold found in [the] treasuries of [the] house of Yahweh and [the] house of the king, and he sent [them] to Hazael king of Aram, and he went up from against Jerusalem.

en.L: And Jehoash king of Judah took all the holy things that Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah his fathers, kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things, and all the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and of the house of the king, and he sent [them] to Hazael king of Aram; and he went up away from Jerusalem.
en.B: So Jehoash king of Judah took all the holy gifts that his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram and Ahaziah, kings of Judah, had dedicated, along with his own holy gifts and all the gold there was in the treasuries of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and of the king's palace, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram. Then Hazael withdrew from Jerusalem.
en.R: So Jehoash king of Judah gathered all the gifts that his ancestors, the kings Jehoshaphat, Jehoram and Ahaziah, had set apart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He added the gifts he himself had set apart and all the gold in the treasuries of the temple and the palace. He sent it all to Hazael king of Aram, and Hazael went away from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the holy things: gifts dedicated to Yahweh
decisions.reason: These are the gifts of silver, gold and other objects that kings had set apart for Yahweh and stored in the temple (1 Kings 15:15). Jehoash used them to buy off the enemy, as Asa had done (1 Kings 15:18).

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah his fathers: the kings of Judah before him
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat was his great-grandfather, Jehoram his grandfather and Ahaziah his father (8:16, 25-26). "Fathers" here means forefathers.

decisions.choice: went up from against Jerusalem: withdrew from attacking it
decisions.reason: "Went up from against" a city is to break off a siege or an attack and leave (1 Kings 15:19). The subject is Hazael.

decisions.choice: the Aramean attack in 2 Chronicles 24
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 24:23-24 tells of an Aramean army that came against Judah and Jerusalem, killed its leaders and defeated Jehoash's larger army. Kings tells only of the payment that turned Hazael away.

decisions.choice: Hazael withdrew
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Hazael as the one who left (m3), since the last person named before the verb is Hazael and "he" could be misread as Jehoash.

source.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹאָ֖שׁ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Joash and all that he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Judah?

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Joash and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
en.B: The rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.
en.R: Everything else Joash did is written in the history of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah: a royal record the writer could consult
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Kings (8:23; 1 Kings 15:7), the writer sends the reader to a fuller written record of Judah's kings, now lost. The question "are they not written ...?" means "they are written".

decisions.choice: Joash: the shorter form of Jehoash
decisions.reason: From here to the end of the chapter the king is called Joash, the shorter form of the same name (verse 1).

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: As in the sources formula throughout these books, Balanced and Readable state as a fact what the Hebrew asks as a question; Literal keeps the question.

decisions.choice: Joash
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the form of the name that this verse uses (m2).

source.text: וַיָּקֻ֥מוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו וַיִּקְשְׁרֽוּ־קָ֑שֶׁר וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת־יוֹאָ֔שׁ בֵּ֥ית מִלֹּ֖א הַיּוֹרֵ֥ד סִלָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose his servants and conspired a conspiracy, and they struck Joash [at] Beth-millo, the [one] going down [to] Silla.

en.L: And his servants arose and conspired a conspiracy, and they struck Joash [at] Beth-millo, which goes down [to] Silla.
en.B: His officials rose up and formed a conspiracy, and they struck down Joash at Beth-millo, on the road that goes down to Silla.
en.R: Some of his officials plotted against Joash. They killed him at Beth-millo, on the way down to Silla.

decisions.choice: his servants: the king's officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants are the men of his court, not household slaves. Verse 22 names two of them.

decisions.choice: Beth-millo ... going down to Silla: a place in Jerusalem, not now known
alternatives: a building on the Millo terrace
decisions.reason: Beth-millo means "house of the Millo". The Millo was a filled terrace or earthwork in the City of David that David and Solomon built up (2 Samuel 5:9; 1 Kings 9:15, 24), and Beth-millo may be a building on it. Silla is not named anywhere else, and the words "which goes down to Silla" may describe a road or a slope leading down from it. Where exactly Joash was killed is not certain.

decisions.choice: the reason for the conspiracy, given in 2 Chronicles 24
decisions.reason: Kings gives no reason. 2 Chronicles 24:20-25 says that after Jehoiada died Joash had Zechariah, Jehoiada's son, stoned to death in the temple court, and his officials conspired against him because of it.

decisions.choice: officials (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are "officials" at Balanced and Readable, as throughout these books; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: on the road that goes down; on the way down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "road" or "way" for what "goes down" (m2), which is uncertain.

source.text: וְיוֹזָבָ֣ד בֶּן־שִׁ֠מְעָת וִיהוֹזָבָ֨ד בֶּן־שֹׁמֵ֤ר׀עֲבָדָיו֙ הִכֻּ֣הוּ וַיָּמֹ֔ת וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in [the] city of David, and reigned Amaziah his son in his place.

en.L: And Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the City of David, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
en.B: It was his officials Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer who struck him down, and he died. He was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Amaziah became king in his place.
en.R: His officials Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer were the ones who killed him. He died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Amaziah became king after him.

decisions.choice: Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer: named a little differently in 2 Chronicles 24:26
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 24:26 calls them Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman. Zabad is a short form of Jozabad, and Shimrith a feminine form of Shomer; Chronicles names their mothers.

decisions.choice: they buried him with his fathers in the City of David
decisions.reason: The usual formula says the king "lay down with his fathers"; here, after a murder, the text says "he died" and then tells of the burial. 2 Chronicles 24:25 adds that he was buried in the City of David but not in the tombs of the kings.

decisions.choice: Amaziah his son: the next king of Judah
decisions.reason: His reign is told in 14:1-22.

decisions.choice: died ... was buried with his ancestors
decisions.reason: The death formula's wording at these levels: "ancestors" for "fathers", and "was buried" because "they buried him" names no one in particular. The verse has "died", not "lay down", and each level says "died".

decisions.choice: It was his officials ... who; were the ones who
decisions.reason: The names stand first in the Hebrew, naming the killers after verse 21; Balanced and Readable keep that weight. "Officials" as in verse 21.
